field_reports.name: Bayside Marine Monterey Bay Report
field_reports.summary: The water conditions were nice and calm but there was some swell. The sea bass are still being caught up the coast. The bluefin are still out near the Canyon edge. The rock fishing is still going good near Davenport in the deep and shallow water. The water conditions look good for tomorrow but that may be a different story Sunday.

field_reports.name: Fishing the North Coast
field_reports.summary: fishingthenorthcoast November 26, 2026 Big Surf, Big Winds, But Where’s the Rain? McKinleyville resident Tatum Brock with a late fall king caught last week while fishing the Smith River. Photo courtesy of Alan Borges/Alan’s Guide Service Big tides, big waves, and big winds pounded the North Coast this week. The only thing missing was the heavy rain that was forecast to hit mid-week. As has been the case all month, the predictions failed to live up to expectations. What we’re left with are coastal rivers teetering between opening and closing. As for the fishing, it’s definitely slowed as the majority of the late-fall kings have either made their way to, or are nearing, their spawning grounds. That’s typical for this time of November. Also typical is a last-minute push of fresh kings riding the next big rise in river levels. Will it happen? The forecasters seem to think so. All of the coastal rivers this week are predicted to reach their highest levels since the rains began in early November. I hope it happens, but consider me skeptical. field_reports.summary: The staff and captains at Dockside Charters would like to wish all of you a Happy Thanksgiving. We all hope that Thanksgiving Day is one that will provide you memories and good times with your family and friends.

field_reports.name: Shake N' Bake Ilwaco Report
field_reports.summary: We went back to the same spot as the day before and found birds and jumpers. We stopped on birds and our sonar lit up but the fish would not bite, except for three dumb ones. What a hit or miss year. ​Mike C 10/12. Good fishing.

field_reports.name: ODFW Ocean Salmon Updates
field_reports.mode: official commercial troll catch and management updates
field_reports.summary: Tomorrow's in-season call with NMFS and the State of Oregon, to discuss Oregon's (SOF) recreational ocean salmon fisheries is cancelled. For the 2026 recreational non-mark selective coho fishery from Cape Falcon to Humbug Mountain, the estimated catch through September 20, 2026, is approximately 22,250 coho salmon, or 87% of the 25,700 quota. The expected coho salmon catch for Saturday September 26, 2026, which was previously adopted and remains open as scheduled, does not provide sufficient balance to add any additional days to the fishery. PREVIOUS ACTION TAKEN: • Effective Saturday, September 26, 2026, from 12:01 a.m. through September 26, 2026, at 11:59 p.m., for the ocean recreational fishery from Cape Falcon to Humbug Mountain, retention of coho salmon is allowed, with a daily bag limit of two salmon (no fin clip requirement). Beginning Sunday, September 27, 2026, the season remains open through October 31, 2026, all salmon, except coho salmon, with a daily bag limit of two salmon. The minimum size for kept Chinook salmon is 24 inches in total length.
